styleSelection.reason: Sargent builds the bow from a few confident transparent washes on dry paper over a pale first wash; pure watercolour, structure from shaped paint, mixed dark accents and reserved cream paper, no ink

families.referenceCue: white bow in airy cool blue: one pale connected wash, then one or two broad cobalt planes (strong left edge, soft darker right side); pale streaks left light; hawse hole a mixed ultramarine and sienna dark, orange rivet dots on dry paper
cream paper left bare, loose pale cobalt strokes; tan and grey rigging diagonals, the two dark round blocks and the orange spar crisp on dry paper
clean sea under a firm horizon: yellow-green near the horizon grading to teal, broken lighter ripples; no warm glaze over it
vertical orange and grey masts and a diagonal spar against pale blue; crisp narrow strokes
clear blue hull of the boat behind with pale streaks; ochre anchor with an orange shank, hard edges against the blue
dark mixed foreground of browns and blue-greens under the bow; darkest at the hull foot but with value steps, not a black slab
